siblings.analysis: C's precondition requires book AntimatterSusdsPair != 0 and == factory.getPair(AM,sUSDS) with code. It cannot tell a seeded pair from a foreign one. In the AP-03 spoof the patcher FILLs the attacker's pair (logs/patcher-spoof.log), so C would pass its precondition and wire UniswapHelper's AM routes to a pair whose price the attacker set. C itself was not executed in this audit.

The ordering hazard is already filed under sya-harvester (pps44-L-am-ordering, Low): A first opens StableStakerV2.claim, AM circulates, and a pre-created pair makes B abort at Step 0. Not re-filed here. B's own side: (a) Step-0 abort on a pre-existing pair is correct fail-loud behaviour on an attended, permissioned path. Nothing has been sent, and seeding into a foreign-priced pair would leak value (AP-01 shows the leak). B has no safe path into an existing pair, and story-113 L405-407 accepts that (no tax-neutral reprice). (b) The ordering ALSO decides whether AP-01/AP-02/AP-03 are reachable at all. Pre-A, no third party holds AM: totalSupply is 0, and no V2 position has reward greater than principal, so the autoAnnihilate excess path is closed. Without AM, a front-runner can only createPair, which is harmless (test_r44_05), or donate sUSDS one-sided, which the attacker loses (test_r44_06). Post-A, AM-cheap pricing steals the seeded AM (AP-01), and AM-dear pricing plus dust LP fakes completion (AP-02/03). Running B strictly BEFORE A is the cheapest operational mitigation.

It defines the minter set [StableStakerV2]. B temporarily adds the seeder and restores the set exactly on every happy-path and resume-matrix run (approvedMinters length 1 after). The exception is a failed tx5 with a foreign pair (AP-02).

pool() between B runs changes the pooler's LP. B persists lp at first sizing, so a resume never re-sizes and never rescues a second slice (resume matrix). The pooler keeps no LP ledger, so the rescue breaks no accounting.

User migrations move phUSD/sUSDS reserves. B's floors are re-read right before the seed in the same local pass. On chain, a reserve move between local pass and tx5 shifts unwrap amounts pro rata (floors -0.1%), so the AM:sUSDS ratio still tracks the live phUSD price. Unwrap amounts can be skewed by swapping in the phUSD/sUSDS pair, but the 0.1% floors bound that to about 0.1%. No finding.
Context only. Rehearsal-fidelity findings are invalid per audit memory.

economics.annihilate: lib/antimatter a5570ce Antimatter.annihilate L253-307: burns `amount` of the caller's AM, pulls the same quantity of a registered stable (rescaled to its decimals), deposits it via PhusdStableMinter (USDC mints 1:1 at the fork), and mints `amount` phUSD for the AM half. Total phUSD = amount + minter(stable). Pause-gated (paused=false at fork).
economics.seededPrice: 0.845161 sUSDS per AM = phUSD's pair price, about $0.942 at sUSDS=1.114576 USDS. This is intended per story-113 L113: 'AM/sUSDS opens at the existing phUSD/sUSDS market price, not at a $1 peg'.
economics.arbitrage: None at the seeded price (test_r44_07: -$14.71 on a 100 sUSDS loop). With phUSD below $1, the stable half of annihilate is loss-making, so AM's annihilate value (2P-1, about $0.884) is below the seeded price. Holders prefer selling into the pool (test_r44_08). The only profitable path is AP-01, buying AM below fair value from an attacker-priced pool.
economics.whoLosesInAP01: Protocol-owned value: 2457.70 phUSD burned from POL. The AM minted in its place ends up with the attacker for about zero sUSDS. The attacker's annihilate re-mints 2452.65 phUSD unbacked by AM-side collateral (plus 2452.65 USDC-backed phUSD).
